relations.subject: server:rebalance

relations.subject: server:node-addition
relations.evidence: All aspects of _provisioning_ that may previously have occurred on the new node are eliminated: this includes buckets, services, and settings.

relations.subject: server:node-join
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, an exact-fit citation: the page states the two are the same operation from opposite ends
relations.evidence: As well as supporting a cluster's adding a node to itself, Couchbase Server also supports a node's joining itself to a cluster (which is essentially the same operation, but proceeding from the node, rather than from the cluster).

relations.subject: server:arbiter-node
relations.evidence: If you do not select any **Services**, Couchbase Server adds the node as an [arbiter node](../../learn/clusters-and-availability/nodes.md#adding-arbiter-nodes).

relations.subject: server:rebalance-retry
relations.evidence: If an unresponsive node become responsive again, rebalance can simply be reattempted manually. Alternatively, the handling of a rebalance-failure can be configured to occur automatically, as described immediately [below](#automated-rebalance-failure-handling).

relations.subject: server:node-addition
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; this dates the node-naming-convention restriction specifically, not node-addition as a whole
relations.evidence: To ensure cluster-security, in Couchbase Server 7.1.1 and later versions, restrictions can be placed on addition, based on the establishment of _node-naming conventions_.

notable_absence.finding: This page never states that node-addition itself is Enterprise-only or Community-only - the only edition-scoped constraint in this whole batch attaches to cluster SIZE (node-management-overview.json) and to address families (manage-address-families.json), not to the add-node operation.

cross_component_finding: REBALANCE ITSELF DOES NOT FRACTURE ON THIS PAGE: the UI, CLI (`couchbase-cli rebalance`) and REST (`POST /controller/rebalance`) surfaces for add-node rebalance are the identical mechanism this page's own cross-references point to from remove-node-and-rebalance.json, join-cluster-and-rebalance.json, failover-graceful.json, failover-hard.json, recover-nodes.json and modify-services-and-rebalance.json - same endpoint, same CLI verb, same vBucket-redistribution description. What DOES genuinely fracture, confirmed across this batch, is the ADMIN OPERATION that precedes and triggers rebalance: node-addition, node-join (its stated inverse), node-removal, failover (itself graceful/hard/auto/unsafe), service-modification and Data-Service reconfiguration are all structurally distinct, separately-gated procedures that happen to converge on one shared rebalance call - exactly the near-miss this round was watching for, but resolved as 'triggers are many, the triggered operation is one' rather than 'rebalance is many things under one name'. server:rebalance-retry (minted here) is itself evidence for this: it retries the ONE rebalance call, regardless of which admin operation queued it.
